title: Keeping watch
heading: Keeping watch
text: Keeping watch An approval describes a use as it was on the day it was decided. Tools change, people leave, approvals run out, and things go wrong. This guide covers what GovWren does to keep the inventory true afterwards, and what it asks of owners, stewards, and governance. For how a request is made and decided in the first place, see Requesting and Reviewing . Who does what: Task Who Confirm the answers at a periodic review The owners of the use Answer an attestation campaign Owners, for their records. Stewards, for their unit's list Declare a change, retire a record, ask for an exception Whoever is responsible for the record: its owners, its unit's stewards, or governance Report an incide

title: Keeping watch
heading: What GovWren does by itself
text: Some work happens on a schedule, without anyone starting it. An administrator sees it under Admin , Scheduled work . Job What it does How often Periodic reviews Opens a review sixty days before an approval ends Every hour Lapsed approvals Marks an approval as lapsed when its end date passes without renewal Every hour Exceptions Ends an exception when its end date passes Every hour Reminders Reminds people of work that is nearly due, and tells the next person up when it is late Every hour Spot checks Draws about one automatic approval in ten for a person to check Every day Email Queues notices and daily summaries, and sends what is waiting Every minute Housekeeping Removes records of job runs

title: Keeping watch
heading: Periodic reviews
text: Every approval has an end date. It comes from the tier: the routing rules give each tier a number of months. In the default program a minimal-tier approval runs for three years and a critical one for six months. Sixty days before the end date, GovWren opens a periodic review. It starts with the owner.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Confirm your answers
text: If you own the use, you are told, and Home lists it under Waiting on you . Open it and choose Confirm for periodic review . You see the request form with the answers given last time already filled in. Go through them. Correct any that are no longer true, then choose Confirm and submit . What happens next depends on the answers as they now stand: The rules say What happens No review is required, and a rule approves it It is approved again at once, with a new end date A review is required It goes to governance for triage, then to reviewers, as a first request does The use keeps its standing while this happens. Standard conditions that still stand are not set a second time. A periodic review, w

title: Keeping watch
heading: If nobody confirms
text: You are reminded fourteen days before the end date. When the date passes, two things happen: the approval is marked Lapsed , and the unit's steward is told that the review is overdue. A lapsed approval shows as lapsed everywhere the use appears, and on everything that relies on it. It is not a decision against the use. Confirming the answers brings it back: when the periodic review approves, the use is approved again. A lapsed approval Governance can decline a periodic review. That ends the approval.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Attestation campaigns
text: A campaign asks the people closest to the work whether the inventory is still true. Governance starts one under Attestations . There are two kinds: Kind Who is asked What they say Owner confirmation The owners of each record in scope Still accurate, changed, or no longer in use Unit completeness The stewards of each unit in scope That the unit's list is complete

title: Keeping watch
heading: Start a campaign
text: Choose Start a campaign . Give it a name, choose what it asks, which part of the organization it covers, and the date answers are wanted by. For an owner confirmation, choose which kinds of record to include: use cases, AI systems, models, or datasets. Everyone it asks is told at once, with how many answers are wanted of them. They are reminded seven days before the date. After the date, an owner's silence is also reported to their unit's steward. A record with no active owner left goes to its unit's steward.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Confirm your records
text: Open the campaign from Home or from the notice. Your records lists what is yours to answer. Tick the records that are still as described, and choose Confirm . Several can be confirmed together. For one that has changed, choose Changed… and say what is different. For a use case this starts a change declaration , and you are taken to the answers to correct them. For one that has ended, choose No longer in use… and say why. The record is retired . Confirming your records in a campaign Each answer is recorded in the history of the record it is about.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Attest that a unit's list is complete
text: In a unit completeness campaign, a steward sees one card for each unit they steward, with what the unit holds. Look at the unit's use cases. If the group uses AI for something that is not there, add it. Then choose Attest that the list is complete . What the unit held at that moment is kept with the attestation.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Read coverage
text: Governance, auditors, and administrators see the whole campaign: the share answered, coverage by unit with the least-answered first, and every record with who it is waiting on. Coverage of an owner confirmation campaign Choose Close the campaign when it has run its course. A closed campaign takes no more answers. What was not answered stays counted as not answered.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Declare a change
text: An approval covers the use as it was described. When that changes, say so before the change, or as soon as you know. On the use case, choose Declare a change and say in a sentence what is changing. You are taken to the request form, with the answers given last time filled in. Correct the ones that are different and choose Submit the change . Declaring a change The rules then judge whether the change is material. It is material if any of these is true: The risk tier is higher than the one approved. The routing rules now require a review that was not required before. An answer that the approval rested on has changed: the purpose, the tool, the data, who is affected, how outputs are used, how m

title: Keeping watch
heading: Retire a record
text: When a use has ended, or a tool, model, or dataset is no longer used, retire it. On the record, choose Retire… and say why. A retired record stays in the inventory with its whole history, marked as retired. Any review of it that was in progress is cancelled, and nothing more falls due for it. The owners of the records that rely on it are told. A use case that uses a retired system, for example, shows that on its own page.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Findings are inherited
text: A record shows what is known about everything it relies on. A use case built on a system that is built on a model inherits what is known about both. These are findings: On a record Shown as An approval that has lapsed, is suspended, or was declined A finding on the use case A tool or model that is not approved, or has been retired A finding on it An open incident A finding on every record the incident involves An exception in force A finding on its record An open risk at the high or critical level A finding on its record. See Assurance Inherited findings appear at the top of the record, marked Inherited from , with the record they come from. Findings on records you may not see are not shown

title: Keeping watch
heading: Exceptions
text: An exception is an approved, time-limited departure from a requirement. Use one when a requirement cannot be met for now and there is a good reason, and something else keeps the risk down meanwhile.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Ask for an exception
text: On the record it applies to, choose Exception… . Say: Which requirement cannot be met. Why it cannot be met for now. What is done instead. When it ends. An exception always ends, and runs for a year at most. Governance is told. Nobody decides an exception they asked for.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Decide an exception
text: Under Exceptions , open the request and choose Approve… or Decline… , with the reason. When approving you may bring the end date forward. An exception, waiting for a decision An exception in force is shown on its record and on everything that relies on that record. Governance can revoke it, with a reason.

title: Keeping watch
heading: When it ends
text: Whoever asked is reminded three weeks before the end date. On the day after the end date the exception ends by itself, and they and governance are told. If more time is needed, choose Ask for more time… . A renewal is a new request, decided afresh, that points to the exception it renews. The register therefore shows how long a departure has really lasted. The exception register

title: Keeping watch
heading: Incidents
text: An incident is something that went wrong with an AI use, or nearly did. Near misses count: they are how a program learns without anyone being harmed.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Report an incident
text: Anyone can report. Under Incidents , choose Report an incident . Say what happened, when, and which records it involves if you know. Describe it; do not paste sensitive data into the report. Governance is told at once. You can follow the incident you reported.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Triage
text: Governance opens the report and chooses Triage… : what kind of incident it is, how serious, and the records it involves. A report that turns out not to be an incident is closed with Not an incident… and the reason, which the reporter sees. Link the record the problem is in. An incident on a model is then shown on every system built on that model and every use of those systems. An incident, with the records it involves and its actions Who sees an incident: governance, auditors, and administrators; whoever reported it; and whoever is responsible for a record it involves.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Suspend an approval, or open a review
text: For a use case the incident involves, governance can: Suspend… its approval, with the reason. The use shows as suspended, and its owners are told. Lift the suspension… when the cause is dealt with. The use goes back to the standing it had. Open a review… of it. An incident review goes to triage with the reviews the rules require. Approving it lifts any suspension. Declining it ends the approval. Neither a suspension nor an incident review restarts the approval period.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Contain and close
text: Choose Mark as contained… and say what was done to stop it. Choose Close… and record the cause and what will be done differently. An incident cannot be closed while an approval it suspended is still suspended.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Actions
text: Everything someone must do, by a date, is in one list under Actions : Actions that governance sets on an incident, each with an owner and a due date. Conditions of a decision that have a date, or that must be met before use. Controls whose check is due, and evidence that has expired or soon will. See When evidence runs out . Mine shows what is yours. Governance, auditors, and administrators can also see Everyone's . Every open action, with its owner and due date When you have done one, choose Done… and say what was done. The owner is reminded a week before the date. When the date passes, governance is told as well.

title: Keeping watch
heading: Committee sessions
text: When the rules send a request to a committee, the decision is made in a meeting. A session records that meeting. Under Sessions , choose Plan a session . Give it a name and a date, and tick the reviews to put on its agenda. Reviews that are ready for a committee decision are ticked for you. A session's agenda The agenda shows, for each review, the tier, how many reviewers objected or asked for conditions, and whether a risk acceptance is still needed. Open the packet to decide. The decision form offers Decided at the session, already ticked, so the decision is recorded as made there. After the meeting, write who attended and the minutes, and choose Close the session . A closed session is a f

title: Keeping watch
heading: Risk acceptance
text: For the highest tier, the default rules say the committee decides and a named person accepts the risk. Such a request cannot be approved until that has happened. The same tier needs an impact assessment from the owner first. In the packet, under Risk acceptance , governance chooses Ask someone to accept it… and picks the person accountable, such as the head of the division. It cannot be someone who made or owns the request. That person is told, and Home lists it. They can read the whole packet, including what reviewers found. They choose Accept the risk… or Decline… and say, in their own words, what they accept or why they do not. The statement is kept with the review, with their name and th

title: Keeping watch
heading: Spot checks
text: Many requests are approved by a rule, with no person involved. A spot check is a second look at a sample of them, to know that the rules decide what a person would. The scheduler draws about one automatic approval in ten. Governance can draw more at any time under Spot checks , with Draw five more . Spot checks of automatic approvals For each one, open the use case, then choose: Agree , if the approval is one you would have made. Disagree… , and say what the rule got wrong. A review of the use opens. Its approval stands until that review is decided. Nobody checks the approval of their own request. The share agreed is a measure of the rules. If it falls, look at which rules approve and change

title: Assurance
heading: Assurance
text: Assurance Deciding requests and keeping the inventory true is most of governance. Assurance is the part that lets you show it: the risks that are known, what is done about each, and what is left. This guide grows with each release. It covers the risk register, the control library, keeping evidence fresh, policies, assessments, and frameworks. Who does what: Task Who Record a risk on a record Whoever is responsible for the record: its owners, its unit's stewards, or governance Record a risk from a review A reviewer of that request Record a risk to the organization Governance Say what is done about a risk, and rescore it Its owner, whoever is responsible for the record, or governance Accept a

title: Assurance
heading: The risk register
text: Risks lists every risk you may see, highest first. Beside the list, a grid counts open risks by how likely and how bad they are, as they stand now. The risk register Who sees a risk: governance, auditors, and administrators see every risk. Anyone else sees the risks they own, and the risks on records they can see in full.

title: Assurance
heading: How a risk is scored
text: A risk has two scores from 1 to 5: how likely it is, and how bad it would be. Their product gives the level. Likelihood times impact Level 1 to 4 Low 5 to 9 Moderate 10 to 16 High 17 to 25 Critical A risk is scored twice. The first score is before anything is done about it. The second is as it stands after treatment. The register and the grid use the second once it is given.

title: Assurance
heading: Record a risk
text: Choose Record a risk . To record one on a record, open the record and choose Risks , then Add a risk . Draw the wording from the library, or write your own. Choose a category, then how likely it is and how bad it would be before anything is done. The risk belongs to whoever records it until an owner is named.

title: Assurance
heading: The risk library
text: GovWren ships about forty risk statements written for research and health settings, in eight categories: Data and privacy Accuracy and reliability Fairness and effects on people Human oversight Security and misuse Suppliers and dependence Research integrity Operations and accountability Each statement says what could go wrong and what usually answers it. A risk drawn from the library keeps a note of which statement it came from. You can change its wording freely; the library is a starting point.

title: Assurance
heading: Say what is done about it
text: Open the risk and choose Say what is done about it… . Choose the treatment: Treatment Meaning Reduce it Something is done that makes it less likely or less bad Pass it to someone else Another party carries it, such as a supplier under an agreement Stop doing what causes it The activity that gives rise to it ends Accept it as it stands Nothing more is done. Only governance may choose this Say what is done and by whom, score the risk as it now stands, and set a date to look at it again. A risk, with its scores before and after treatment On that date the owner is reminded. Setting a new date asks again when it comes.

title: Assurance
heading: A risk from a review
text: A reviewer who finds something that will outlast the review can record it as a risk, from the review. It is attached to the use case and goes to the use's accountable owner, with the review it came from noted on it.

title: Assurance
heading: Risks are findings
text: An open risk at the two highest levels is shown at the top of its record. Like an incident or an exception, it is also shown on everything that relies on that record, marked as inherited. See Findings are inherited . Treating a risk down to moderate or low removes it from there. It stays in the register.

title: Assurance
heading: Close a risk
text: When a risk no longer applies, governance closes it with the reason. A closed risk keeps its history and is left out of the grid.

title: Assurance
heading: Controls
text: A control is a safeguard: something the program does, or something that must be true of a use, a tool, or a model. GovWren ships a library of about thirty, written from what a governance program has to do. It stands on its own; no outside framework is needed to use it. The library has eight groups: Know what is in use Name who answers for it Match review to risk Keep data where it may be Keep people in the loop Hold suppliers to terms Respond when something goes wrong Keep the record The control library

title: Assurance
heading: Two kinds of control
text: Kind Applies to Who says how it stands Program control The program as a whole, once Governance Record control Every record its rule picks out Whoever is responsible for each record A control is defined once. A record control is not copied to each record: whether it applies is worked out from the record each time. A control that asks for a tested way to stop a system, for example, applies to use cases at the high tier and above. If a use rises to that tier, the control applies from then on.

title: Assurance
heading: The controls of a record
text: On a record, choose Controls . You see the controls that apply to it, by group, each with how it stands there. The controls of one use case Choose Set… on one and say how it stands: Standing Meaning Not started Nothing has been done yet. This is where every control begins In progress Partly done In place Done. Say how it is done here Does not apply The rule picked this record out, but the control makes no sense for it. Only governance may say so, with the reason

title: Assurance
heading: Checking that a control is still in place
text: Marking a control as in place sets the date of its next check, from the control's own cadence: three, six, or twelve months. On that date the owner is reminded, and the control shows Check is due . To record a check, choose Set… , tick I checked today that it is still in place , and save. The next check moves on by the same cadence.

title: Assurance
heading: Evidence for a control
text: Once a control has a standing on a record, choose Attach beside it to attach what shows it is in place: a signed procedure, a test report, a screenshot of a setting. Evidence can carry a date it is good until. See Keep evidence . A control that is in place shows: No evidence when nothing is attached. Evidence expired when everything attached has passed its date.

title: Assurance
heading: When evidence runs out
text: The owner of a piece of evidence is told sixty days before it expires, and again when it has. Both appear in their action list , along with: Each control of theirs whose check is due. Each control in place whose evidence has all expired. So a gap in assurance is something a named person has been asked to close, not something an auditor finds.

title: Assurance
heading: One control across the inventory
text: Open a control from the library to see every record it applies to and how it stands on each, with those not started first. One control, across the records it applies to

title: Assurance
heading: Controls and risks
text: Each control names the risks from the library that it answers. A risk drawn from the library shows those controls on its page, with how each stands for the record the risk is on. A risk that is scored high with none of its controls in place is the first place to look.

title: Assurance
heading: Policies
text: A policy is one of the organization's own rules: acceptable use, AI in research, data about people. GovWren keeps each policy's text with its versions, its owner, the date it is next reviewed, and the controls that carry it out. Everyone signed in can read the policies in force, under Policies . Policies in force

title: Assurance
heading: Write and publish a policy
text: Choose Start a policy and give it a name. It is a draft, and only governance, auditors, and administrators can see it. Choose Write a new version and write the text. Leave a blank line between paragraphs, and start a line with ## for a heading. Then choose Publish . The policy is in force from then on. To change a policy, write a new version and say what changed. The version in force stays as it is until the new one is published. Published versions are never edited, and each stays on the record with its date.

title: Assurance
heading: Owner, review date, and controls
text: Under Details… , set who owns the policy, the date it is next reviewed, and the controls that carry it out. On that date the owner is reminded, and the policy shows Review is due . Linking controls answers the question an assurer asks of every policy: how do you know it is followed? The policy shows its controls, and each control shows how it stands. A policy, with its controls and acknowledgments

title: Assurance
heading: Ask people to acknowledge it
text: Choose Ask for acknowledgment… . Choose a unit, which includes the units beneath it, or everyone, and the date to acknowledge by. Each person is told, and Home lists it. They open the policy, read it, and choose I have read it . They are reminded a week before the date and once after it. The policy shows how many of those asked have acknowledged it, by unit, with the lowest first. An acknowledgment is of one version. When a new version is published, nobody has acknowledged it yet; ask again if the change matters enough.

title: Assurance
heading: Retire a policy
text: Retire takes a policy out of force. It stays on the record with its versions, and is no longer shown to everyone.

title: Assurance
heading: Assessments
text: An assessment is a set of structured answers about one record. GovWren ships two. Assessment About When Impact assessment A use case When the rules require it, or whenever its owner chooses Vendor due diligence A vendor Before its tools are approved for anything sensitive Each is drafted, submitted, and then reviewed by governance. A submitted assessment can be corrected until it is reviewed. After that it is fixed, and answering again starts a new one.

title: Assurance
heading: Impact assessment
text: An impact assessment asks who could be affected by a use, what the worst realistic outcome is, whether it could work less well for some groups, and what is done about each: who checks the output, how people are told, and how someone can ask for a person to look again. By default the rules require one for every request at the critical tier. Such a request cannot be approved until its owner has submitted the assessment. The owner opens it from the use case, with Impact assessment , or from the notice on the review. Reviewers and the committee read it from the decision packet. An impact assessment The assessment is kept with the review it was made for and stays in the history of the use. The ru

title: Assurance
heading: Vendor due diligence
text: On a vendor, choose Due diligence . The questionnaire asks what a supplier does with what customers enter, how long it keeps it and where, what security assurance it holds, how it gives notice of changes to its models, and whether an agreement covers all of that. Attach the assurances the supplier gives, such as a security report, as evidence on the vendor. Vendor due diligence Submitting the questionnaire marks the vendor's due diligence as in progress. When a second person in governance reviews it, the vendor's due diligence is complete.

title: Assurance
heading: Frameworks
text: A framework is someone else's list of requirements: a standard, a regulator's guidance, a funder's terms. GovWren does not need one. The control library stands on its own, and everything above works with no framework loaded. Load a framework when you are asked to show how your program answers it.

title: Assurance
heading: Load a framework
text: Under Frameworks , the built-in frameworks that are not loaded are listed. Choose Load it . GovWren ships one: the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, as its four functions and nineteen categories, each summarized in a sentence. The subcategories are not included; read the framework itself for its full text. A framework is a data file, called a pack. It holds the requirements, each with a code, and a crosswalk from requirement codes to controls in the library. To load your own, send the pack to the API : POST /api/v1/frameworks with the document as pack . A pack that names a control that is not in the library, or a requirement that is not in the pack, is refused whole, with what is wrong. Loa

title: Assurance
heading: Read readiness
text: Open a framework to see where the program stands against it. Nothing here is typed in. Each requirement takes its state from the controls mapped to it: State Meaning Covered Every control mapped to it is in place, with evidence that is still good Partly covered Some are, or a control is in place with no evidence, or with evidence that has expired A gap None of its controls is in place Not mapped No control is mapped to it. This is its own state and is never counted as covered Does not apply Governance has said so, with the reason A program control counts as fully in place when it is marked in place and has evidence that has not expired. A record control counts by the share of the records it

title: Assurance
heading: The statement of applicability
text: Statement of applicability , on the Frameworks page, downloads the whole control library as a spreadsheet: each control, whether it applies and why, how it stands, who owns it, and the evidence behind it. It needs no framework to be loaded. The same list is available from the API at GET /api/v1/statement-of-applicability , as CSV or, with format=json , as JSON.

title: Configuration
heading: Configuration
text: Configuration This guide is for whoever runs the server. It covers govwren.toml , environment overrides, the data home, PostgreSQL, running behind a reverse proxy, and the guard on demo installations.

title: Configuration
heading: What is configured where
text: GovWren keeps two kinds of settings apart. Kind Where it lives Examples How the server runs govwren.toml and the environment Address, port, database, data home The program and the product's look The database, set in the app or by a program pack Forms, risk tiers, routing rules, vocabularies, name, logo, colors This guide is about the first. For the second, see Running the program .

title: Configuration
heading: Where the file is found
text: uv run govwren init writes a commented govwren.toml in the current directory. Every command looks for the file in this order: The --config FILE option (short form -c ), given before the command. The GOVWREN_CONFIG environment variable. ./govwren.toml . uv run govwren --config /etc/govwren/govwren.toml doctor Relative paths in the file are resolved against the file's own directory, not the directory you run from. An installation therefore moves as a unit.

title: Configuration
heading: Every section and key
text: The file has five sections. A section or key that GovWren does not know is an error, not something it ignores. Every problem in the file is reported together.

title: Configuration
heading: [server]
text: Key Default Meaning host "127.0.0.1" The address the web server listens on. Keep 127.0.0.1 when a reverse proxy on the same machine terminates TLS. Use 0.0.0.0 only behind one port 8000 The port, from 1 to 65535 workers 1 How many server processes to run, from 1 to 64. One is enough for SQLite and small teams base_url "" The public address people use to reach GovWren, such as "https://govwren.example.org" , with no path. Used for links in email and for the single sign-on redirect address. Set it once people reach GovWren at a stable address session_idle_hours 12 A sign-in ends after this long without activity. At least 1 session_max_days 7 A sign-in ends after this long in any case. At least

title: Configuration
heading: [database]
text: Key Default Meaning url "" Empty means SQLite, in the file govwren.db inside the data home. For PostgreSQL, an address beginning postgresql+psycopg:// . See Use PostgreSQL

title: Configuration
heading: [data]
text: Key Default Meaning home "var" The data home: the one directory that holds everything not in the database

title: Configuration
heading: [sso]
text: Single sign-on through an OpenID Connect provider. It is off until issuer and client_id are set. The keys are listed in Single sign-on .

title: Configuration
heading: [mail]
text: Email over SMTP. It is off until host and from_address are set. The keys are listed in Email .

title: Configuration
heading: The file as written by init
text: With its comments left out: [server] host = "127.0.0.1" port = 8000 workers = 1 base_url = "" session_idle_hours = 12 session_max_days = 7 scheduler = true [database] url = "" [data] home = "var" GovWren also gives advice that does not stop it running. serve and doctor warn when several workers share one SQLite file, and when base_url is http:// on a host other than localhost.

title: Configuration
heading: Environment overrides
text: Any value can be overridden by an environment variable named GOVWREN_<SECTION>_<KEY> , in capitals. The environment wins over the file. Variable Overrides GOVWREN_SERVER_HOST [server] host GOVWREN_SERVER_PORT [server] port GOVWREN_SERVER_WORKERS [server] workers GOVWREN_SERVER_BASE_URL [server] base_url GOVWREN_SERVER_SESSION_IDLE_HOURS [server] session_idle_hours GOVWREN_SERVER_SESSION_MAX_DAYS [server] session_max_days GOVWREN_SERVER_SCHEDULER [server] scheduler GOVWREN_DATABASE_URL [database] url GOVWREN_DATA_HOME [data] home GOVWREN_SERVER_PORT=8080 uv run govwren serve Numbers are read from the variable's text, so 8080 works without quotes. GOVWREN_CONFIG is separate: it names the file

title: Configuration
heading: Secrets are refused in the file
text: govwren.toml is meant to be safe to read, copy, and keep under version control. GovWren refuses to start if the file holds a secret: A key named password , secret , token , api_key , or key , or ending in one of those after an underscore, is an error wherever it appears. A database address with a password in it is an error when it is written in the file. Put secrets in the environment instead. For the database, set the password in PGPASSWORD , or put the whole address, password and all, in GOVWREN_DATABASE_URL .

title: Configuration
heading: The data home
text: The data home is created by init . With the default settings it is ./var . Path Holds govwren.db The SQLite database, when no database address is set brand/ Uploaded logos and the tab icon logs/ govwren.log , rotated at about 5 MB, with five older files kept files/ Evidence files, each stored once under the SHA-256 of its content. Back this up with the database: the database says what each file is, and this directory holds it exports/ Reserved for exports .govwren-home A marker that says this directory is a data home Back it up as a whole. With PostgreSQL, back up the database as well. Do not edit its contents by hand. It must be writable by the account that runs the server. Request bodies a

title: Configuration
heading: Use PostgreSQL
text: SQLite is the default and needs no setup. Use PostgreSQL when many people will use GovWren at once or you want more than one server process. The features and the data model are the same on both. Install the driver, which is optional: `` bash uv sync --extra postgres `` Create an empty database and a role that owns it, with your usual PostgreSQL tools. Set the address in govwren.toml , without the password: `` toml [database] url = "postgresql+psycopg://govwren@db.example.org:5432/govwren" `` Put the password in the environment, then set up and check: `` bash export PGPASSWORD='the database password' uv run govwren init uv run govwren doctor `` init creates the schema, loads the default progr

title: Configuration
heading: Run behind a reverse proxy
text: GovWren serves plain HTTP. For anything beyond your own machine, put a reverse proxy in front of it to terminate TLS. Keep host = "127.0.0.1" , so that only the proxy can reach GovWren. Have the proxy forward every path to http://127.0.0.1:8000 . Have the proxy pass these headers: Header Why Host , or X-Forwarded-Host GovWren refuses changes whose Origin does not match the host it was asked for. If the proxy rewrites Host , it must send the public name in X-Forwarded-Host X-Forwarded-Proto: https So that the session cookie is marked Secure Set base_url to the public address, such as "https://govwren.example.org" . What GovWren does itself, so the proxy need not: It sends a strict content sec

title: Configuration
heading: The demo and the network
text: A demo organization offers sign-in as any of its sample people with no password. That is safe on your own machine and nowhere else, so two guards apply. serve refuses to start a demo on any address other than 127.0.0.1 , localhost , or ::1 . Passwordless sign-in is answered only for callers on the same machine. To let a demo be reached from other machines, for example to show it to colleagues on a trusted network, say so explicitly: uv run govwren --config demo/govwren.toml serve --host 0.0.0.0 --demo-on-network --demo-on-network lifts both guards for that run. Anyone who can reach the server can then sign in as any sample person, including its administrator. Do not use it on a network you d

title: Configuration
heading: Check your settings
text: uv run govwren doctor doctor reads the configuration the same way the server does, so it is the quickest way to find a mistake. It reports the file it used, any advice, the data home, the database and its schema, and whether the history verifies.

title: Single sign-on
heading: Single sign-on
text: Single sign-on GovWren can let people sign in with the account your organization already gives them, through any identity provider that speaks OpenID Connect. This guide sets it up, with the exact steps for Microsoft Entra ID, and explains how the provider's groups become roles in GovWren. Single sign-on is optional. Without it, people sign in with a password that GovWren keeps, as described in Getting started .

title: Single sign-on
heading: How it works
text: A person chooses Sign in with your organization account on the sign-in page. GovWren sends the browser to your identity provider, which signs the person in as it always does. The provider sends the browser back with a one-time code. GovWren exchanges the code for a signed ID token and checks its signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and that it answers this sign-in and no other. GovWren finds the person's account, or creates it, and gives them the roles their groups map to. GovWren uses the authorization code flow with PKCE. It accepts ID tokens signed with RS256 and refuses anything else. It never sees the person's password.

title: Single sign-on
heading: What you need
text: GovWren reachable at a stable https address, set as base_url in the [server] section of govwren.toml . The provider sends people back to <base_url>/api/v1/sso/callback . The right to register an application with your identity provider. A local administrator account in GovWren. You keep it as the way in if the provider is ever unreachable.

title: Single sign-on
heading: Set it up with Microsoft Entra ID

title: Single sign-on
heading: 1. Register GovWren
text: In the Entra admin center, under App registrations , choose New registration . Field Value Name GovWren Supported account types Accounts in this organizational directory only Redirect URI Platform Web , address https://govwren.example.org/api/v1/sso/callback (your own address) After it is created, note two values from its Overview page: the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID .

title: Single sign-on
heading: 2. Create a client secret
text: Under Certificates & secrets , add a New client secret . Copy its Value now; it is shown once. Note when it expires: sign-in stops working on that day until you replace it.

title: Single sign-on
heading: 3. Send groups or application roles in the token
text: GovWren reads one claim from the ID token to learn what a person belongs to. Choose one of these. Application roles (recommended). Under App roles , create a role for each kind of access, for example Governance , Auditor , PrivacyReviewer . Then, under Enterprise applications → GovWren → Users and groups , assign people or groups to those roles. Entra sends them in a claim named roles , by the role's Value . Names are stable and readable, and only what you assigned is sent. Security groups. Under Token configuration , choose Add groups claim and select Security groups for the ID token. Entra sends them in a claim named groups , by each group's object ID. If a person is in more groups than fi

title: Single sign-on
heading: 4. Tell GovWren
text: In govwren.toml : [server] base_url = "https://govwren.example.org" [sso] issuer = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/YOUR-TENANT-ID/v2.0" client_id = "YOUR-APPLICATION-CLIENT-ID" groups_claim = "roles" # or "groups", if you chose security groups trust_email = true Put the client secret in the environment of the GovWren server, never in the file: export GOVWREN_SSO_CLIENT_SECRET='the secret value' Then check and restart: uv run govwren doctor doctor reads the provider's discovery document and says whether the secret is set. trust_email = true is right for a single-tenant registration, because every address the tenant sends belongs to the person signing in. Entra does not mark addresses as ve

title: Single sign-on
heading: 5. Map groups to roles
text: Sign in to GovWren as an administrator and open Admin → Single sign-on . The page shows the connection and the redirect address to register. Under Groups and roles , add a line for each group or application role: Group or application role Role in GovWren For Governance Governance Everywhere Auditor Auditor Everywhere PrivacyReviewer Reviewer Privacy NeuroscienceLeads Steward of a unit Neuroscience HaleLab Member of a unit Hale Lab Enter each value exactly as the provider sends it: the role's Value for application roles, or the object ID for security groups. Admin → Single sign-on, before a provider is connected

title: Single sign-on
heading: How accounts and roles behave
text: A person is recognized by the provider's own identifier for them (the token's subject), not by their email address. Changing someone's address at the provider does not create a second account. A first sign-in joins an existing account when the address the provider vouches for matches one an administrator created or imported earlier. Otherwise a new account is created, as an ordinary member. Roles from the provider are set again at every sign-in. Remove someone from a group and the role goes the next time they sign in. Add them and it appears. Roles given by hand under Admin → People are left alone. The two kinds are kept apart. Membership of a unit is added, never removed, by a mapping. Remo

title: Single sign-on
heading: Turn off passwords
text: Once single sign-on works, you can stop password sign-in for everyone except administrators: [sso] local_sign_in = false Administrators keep their passwords as the way in when the provider cannot be reached. Keep at least one such account, with a long password stored somewhere safe.

title: Single sign-on
heading: Settings
text: Key in [sso] Default Meaning issuer "" The provider's issuer address. Empty turns single sign-on off client_id "" The identifier the provider gave GovWren client_secret_env "GOVWREN_SSO_CLIENT_SECRET" The name of the environment variable that holds the client secret scopes "openid profile email" What GovWren asks the provider for. title: Email
heading: Email
text: Email GovWren can send its notices by email: a request that needs triage, a review task, a question from a reviewer, a decision, an answer about a tool someone asked for. Each person chooses whether to get them as they happen, once a day as a summary, or not at all. Email is optional. Without it, everything that needs a person is on their Home page and under the bell, exactly as before.

title: Email
heading: How sending works
text: Nothing is sent straight from the click that caused it. A notice is written to the database with the change that caused it. The mailer, which runs inside the server, picks notices up, writes each message to an outbox in the same database, and sends from there. So: a restart loses nothing; a mail server that is down is tried again after 5 minutes, then 10, 20, 40, and 80, and given up on after six attempts, with the reason kept; several server processes never send the same message twice, because each message is claimed before it is sent. If you prefer to send from a scheduled job, or the server is not running, send what is waiting with: uv run govwren mail run It exits with 1 if anything coul

title: The API
heading: The API
text: API Everything the web app does, it does through GovWren's JSON API. You can use the same API to connect another system. This guide covers the conventions and the main routes. The exact shape of every request and response is in the OpenAPI document.

title: The API
heading: The basics
text: Base path /api/v1 Format JSON in, JSON out Sign-in A session cookie, set by POST /api/v1/session Changes Need the X-CSRF-Token header Success {"data": …, "meta": …} Errors A problem document, application/problem+json OpenAPI docs/openapi.json in the repository, and /api/openapi.json on a running server The API is not cached: every API response carries Cache-Control: no-store . The server does not serve interactive API documentation pages. Load the OpenAPI document into a viewer of your choice. This release has no API keys or tokens for other systems. A script signs in as an account, as shown below, and can do exactly what that account's roles allow. Give a script its own account with the lea

title: The API
heading: Sign in
text: Send an email address and password. The answer sets the session cookie, govwren_session , and returns who you are, your roles, and a CSRF token. curl -s -c cookies.txt \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"email": "you@example.org", "password": "your password"}' \ http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/session { "data": { "account": {"id": 1, "name": "Your Name", "email": "you@example.org"}, "roles": ["governance", "member"], "permissions": {"admin": false, "govern": true, "configure": true, "read_all": true, "edit_all": true, "review": true, "steward": false}, "steward_units": [], "member_units": [], "has_password": true, "csrf_token": "…" }, "meta": {} } The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=S

title: The API
heading: Send the CSRF token with every change
text: Every request that is not a GET , HEAD , or OPTIONS must carry the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header. Without it the answer is 403. Signing in and signing out are the exceptions. curl -s -b cookies.txt \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'X-CSRF-Token: THE_TOKEN' \ -d '{"name": "Brightfen Labs"}' \ http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/vendors GovWren also refuses changes that come from another site in a browser: a request whose Origin header does not match the host it was sent to, or that the browser marks as cross-site, answers 403. A command-line client sends no Origin header and is not affected.

title: The API
heading: Responses
text: Every successful answer is an envelope with two keys: {"data": {"ref": "VND-0041", "name": "Brightfen Labs", "status": "prospective", "version": 1}, "meta": {}} data is the thing you asked for: an object or a list. meta holds facts about the answer, such as paging. It is an empty object when there is nothing to say. The example is shortened; a real record has more fields. A route that creates a record answers 201. Records are named by their permanent reference, such as UC-0142 , SYS-0007 , VND-0041 , or RV-0087 , not by a numeric id. People and units are named by numeric id.

title: The API
heading: Errors
text: Every error is a problem document with the media type application/problem+json . { "type": "about:blank", "title": "Forbidden", "status": 403, "detail": "The request is missing its CSRF token. Reload the page.", "instance": "/api/v1/vendors" } When particular fields are at fault, an errors list says which: { "type": "about:blank", "status": 422, "detail": "The decision was not recorded.", "instance": "/api/v1/reviews/RV-0087/decision", "errors": [ {"location": ["rationale"], "message": "Give the reason for the decision. It is shown to the requester."} ] } (The title is left out of this example.) detail and message are written to be shown to a person. Status Meaning 400 The request could not

title: The API
heading: Change a record safely
text: To change a use case, AI system, or vendor, send a PATCH with only the fields that change and the version you were looking at. curl -s -b cookies.txt -X PATCH \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'X-CSRF-Token: THE_TOKEN' \ -d '{"version": 1, "website": "https://brightfen.example"}' \ http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/vendors/VND-0041 If someone else has saved the record since, the answer is 409 and nothing is changed. Fetch the record again, and repeat your change with the new version . Every change is written to the history against the account that made it.

title: Command reference
heading: Command reference
text: Command reference Every govwren command. This page is written from the program itself, so it always matches the version it ships with. Run commands with uv run govwren … from the project directory. Options that come before the command apply to all of them: govwren [-h] [--version] [-c FILE] [-v | -q] COMMAND ...

title: Command reference
heading: Commands
text: Command What it does govwren init Set up a new installation govwren serve Run the web server govwren demo Build a fictional organization to explore govwren db Look after the database schema govwren users Manage accounts from the command line govwren jobs List scheduled work, or run what is due govwren mail Send waiting email, or test the mail settings govwren program Export or load the governance program as a file govwren verify Check that the history has not been altered govwren doctor Check that this installation is healthy

title: Command reference
heading: govwren init
text: Write a configuration file if there is none, create the data home, create or upgrade the database, and create the first administrator if there is none. Safe to run again. Option Meaning --force overwrite an existing configuration file --admin-email EMAIL create the first administrator with this address --admin-name NAME the first administrator's name --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking

title: Command reference
heading: govwren serve
text: Run GovWren's web server. It refuses to start on a database whose schema is behind; run govwren db upgrade first. Option Meaning --host address to listen on (default: from the configuration) --port PORT port to listen on (default: from the configuration) --workers WORKERS server processes (default: from the configuration) --reload restart when the code changes (development) --demo-on-network let a demo organization listen beyond this machine (anyone who reaches it can sign in as its sample people)

title: Command reference
heading: govwren demo
text: Build the Alderpoint Institute for Medical Research, a fictional organization with thirty months of history, in its own directory. Everything in it is made by the same code the app uses. Start it with the command it prints. text: Manage accounts from the command line: for setting up, and for getting back in when nobody can sign in. Everyday account management is in the app, under Admin. Changes made here are recorded in the history as made at the command line.

title: Command reference
heading: govwren users add
text: Add an account. It asks for a password unless --password-stdin or --invite is given. Option Meaning EMAIL the email address the person signs in with --name the person's name --title their job title --role ROLE a role: admin, governance, auditor, reviewer, reviewer=function:KEY, or steward=unit:CODE (may be repeated) --unit CODE a unit they work in, by code (may be repeated) --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking --invite add them without a password: they can be named on records now, and sign in once they are given a password or use single sign-on

title: Command reference
heading: govwren users list
text: List every account with its status and roles.

title: Command reference
heading: govwren users disable
text: Stop an account signing in and end its sessions. Its records and history are kept. The last active administrator cannot be disabled. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address

title: Command reference
heading: govwren users enable
text: Let a disabled account sign in again. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address

title: Command reference
heading: govwren users reset-password
text: Give an account a new password and end its sessions. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking

title: Command reference
heading: govwren users roles
text: Show an account's roles, or with --set replace the roles granted in GovWren. Roles mapped from an identity provider are left alone. The last active administrator cannot lose that role. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address --set ROLE a role: admin, governance, auditor, reviewer, reviewer=function:KEY, or steward=unit:CODE (may be repeated); with none, removes every role

title: Command reference
heading: govwren jobs
text: GovWren does some work by itself: it opens periodic reviews, marks approvals that have run out, sends reminders, and sends email. The server does this while it runs. With no command, this lists each job and when it is next due.

title: Command reference
heading: govwren jobs run
text: Run every job that is due, once, and exit. Give a job's name to run that one now whether or not it is due. Safe to run while the server is up: a job is never run by two processes at once. Exits with 1 if a job failed. Option Meaning JOB the job to run now

title: Command reference
heading: govwren mail
text: The server sends email by itself while it runs. These commands are for testing the settings, and for sending what is waiting when the server is not running.

title: Command reference
heading: govwren mail run
text: Turn waiting notices into messages, put together daily summaries if it is time, and send what is in the outbox. Exits with 1 if anything could not be sent.

title: Command reference
heading: govwren mail test
text: Send one message now, to the address of an existing account, and say whether the mail server accepted it. Option Meaning EMAIL the account to send it to

title: Command reference
heading: govwren program
text: The governance program (forms, the scoring model, and vocabularies) can be written out as one file, kept under version control, reviewed, and loaded into another installation.

title: Command reference
heading: govwren program export
text: Write the published forms, the scoring model, and every vocabulary as one program pack. Option Meaning --out FILE write to this file instead of the screen

title: Command reference
heading: govwren program import
text: Load a program pack. The whole file is checked first, and nothing is loaded if anything is wrong. What differs from the published program becomes a new version; earlier versions are kept, so past requests still show the form they were answered on. Option Meaning FILE the pack to load --check check the file and change nothing

title: Command reference
heading: govwren verify
text: Recompute the hash chain over every event in the history and report the first one that does not hold. Exits with 1 if the history is broken.

title: Command reference
heading: govwren doctor
text: Check the configuration, the data home, the database and its schema, and the history. Exits with 1 if anything must be fixed.

title: Changelog
heading: Changelog

title: Changelog
text: Wave 4, Assurance : show that the program's safeguards exist and work. A risk register, a control library with evidence, policies, assessments, and optional readiness against a framework.

title: Changelog
heading: Upgrading from 0.3.0
text: Run govwren db upgrade (migrations 0018 to 0022). Every row is kept and the history still verifies. The upgrade loads the risk library and the control library; nothing you have set up is touched. One rule is new. A request at the critical tier now needs an impact assessment from its owner before it can be approved. Reviews of such requests that are open when you upgrade need one too. To require it at another tier, or not at all, change required_when in the assessments pack. No framework is loaded by the upgrade. Frameworks are optional.

title: Changelog
heading: Added
text: The risk register: risks on a record or on the organization, scored before and after treatment on two five-point scales, owned, and looked at again on a date. A grid counts open risks by likelihood and impact. A risk library of about forty statements written for research and health settings, loaded as a pack. A risk drawn from it keeps its source. A control library of about thirty safeguards, loaded as a pack. A control applies to the program, or to every record its rule picks out; it is never copied per record. Each applicable control has a standing, an owner, and a date it is next checked, and each names the risks it answers. Evidence attached to a control's standing. Owners are told befor

title: Changelog
text: Wave 3, Keeping watch : the inventory stays true as time passes. GovWren now acts when something is due, asks the people closest to the work whether the record is still right, and records what goes wrong and what is done about it.

title: Changelog
heading: Upgrading from 0.2.0
text: Run govwren db upgrade (migrations 0013 to 0017). Every row is kept and the history still verifies. The server now does scheduled work by itself. The first time it runs after the upgrade it catches up on everything that is already due: Every approval whose end date has passed is marked lapsed. A periodic review opens for every approval that ends within sixty days, or has ended. One reminder goes out for each review task, condition, and confirmation that is nearly due or overdue. On an installation that has run for some time this can be many notices at once. title: Changelog
heading: Changed
text: The mailer is now one of the scheduled jobs. govwren mail run still works. Once a request has been decided, its owners change what it says by declaring a change, where before they had to ask governance. The side menu has a new group, Keeping watch, for actions, incidents, attestations, and exceptions. [server] scheduler , which is true unless set otherwise, says whether the server runs scheduled work.

title: Changelog
heading: Added
text: A scheduler in the server, with govwren jobs and an Admin page. A job is claimed in the database before it runs, so several processes never run the same one at once. Periodic reviews: sixty days before an approval ends, a review opens with the owner, who confirms or corrects the earlier answers. Unchanged, low-risk uses are approved again on the spot; the rest go to reviewers. Lapsed approvals: an approval that passes its end date without renewal is marked lapsed, with the reason in its history, and comes back when a periodic review approves it. Reminders before review tasks, conditions, and confirmations are due, and escalation after: to governance for a review task, to the unit's steward f

title: Changelog
text: Wave 2, System of record : a connected inventory of use cases, systems, models, agents, datasets, and vendors; single sign-on; email; and a program that governance edits itself.

title: Changelog
heading: Upgrading from 0.1.0
text: Run govwren db upgrade (migrations 0007 to 0012). Every row is kept and the history still verifies. Two things stay as they were until you choose otherwise: The request form. An installation keeps the form it has. The questions about models people run or train themselves are in the default program shipped with this release; add them under Governance, Program, or load the default pack. Email and single sign-on are off until you give them settings. No runtime dependency was added in this release.

title: Changelog
heading: Added
text: Single sign-on. Sign-in through any OpenID Connect provider, using the authorization code flow with PKCE. ID tokens are checked for signature (RS256), issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce. Accounts are created at first sign-in and recognized afterwards by the provider's own identifier, never by an unverified address. An administrator maps the provider's groups or application roles to roles, unit stewardship, unit membership, and review functions under Admin, Single sign-on; mapped roles are set again at every sign-in and roles given by hand are left alone. A mapping never removes the last administrator. Password sign-in can be kept for administrators only. govwren doctor checks the connection

title: Changelog
text: Wave 1, Front door : install, sign in, and take a request from "may I use this?" through tiering, review, and a recorded decision; register a catalog tool in a minute.

title: Changelog
heading: Added
text: Foundation. govwren init , serve , db upgrade , db current , verify , and doctor . Deployment settings in govwren.toml with environment overrides; secrets are refused in the file. A data home for files. SQLite by default and PostgreSQL by address, on one model and one set of migrations (migration 0001). History. Every change to a record is written to an append-only history in the same transaction, with who, when, and each value before and after. Events are chained by hash; govwren verify finds the first event that has been altered, removed, or cut from the end. The database itself refuses updates and deletes on the history.
